title: Michael Brennan wins Wyndham Championship, qualifies for FedEx Cup playoffs
content:
Another week, another PGA Tour winner in their early twenties: Michael Brennan, 24, won the Wyndham Championship on Sunday by three shots to cap off the tour’s regular season and earn his way into post-season play.

He is the third consecutive champion under the age of 25, following 21-year-old Jackson Koivun’s win at the 3M Open and 24-year-old Michael Thorbjornsen’s triumph at the Rocket Classic.

With the victory, Brennan surged from outside the top 100 to No. 47 in the FedEx Cup standings — well inside the top-70 threshold to qualify for the playoffs, which begin next week.

“It’s everything,” Brennan said of the win and his playoff berth. “I don’t want to be done playing golf; I feel like I’ve played the best golf I have all year in the last couple weeks. Unfortunately, a couple tough Sundays, but outside of that, I’ve been playing really, really solid. This is my sixth week (playing) in a row, so seven is a lot, but I think I’m going to be perfectly happy to be running on fumes next week.”

Brennan, 24, claimed his second PGA Tour victory at Sedgefield Country Club, a venue less than 30 miles away from his alma mater, Wake Forest University. He started Sunday’s round tied for the lead with Beau Hossler before making five birdies in a row on his front nine to pull away. One of those birdies came after a near-ace on the 211-yard par-3 7th. Brennan hit his tee shot to 6 inches.

The nerves kicked in on Brennan’s back nine as he held a three-shot lead over Hossler headed into his final four holes. But he scraped together pars after wayward tee shots on No. 15 and No. 17, fending off a late charge from Hossler, who birdied the 17th. Hossler, projected outside of that coveted top-70 at the time of the group’s penultimate hole, needed a win to extend his season. Brennan needed a three-way tie for second place, or better, according to the PGA Tour’s projections.

On No. 18, with a two-shot lead, Brennan striped his tee shot down the middle and stuck his approach to 13 feet. He sank the putt and unleashed a passionate fist bump with his parents watching nearby. As Hossler finished his hole, Brennan put his arm around his caddie, Olly Brett, whom he hired away from LPGA Tour winner Rose Zhang early this year.

Brennan burst onto the tour in 2025 when he won in his first career start playing as a sponsor’s exemption at the Bank of Utah Championship. His game began to trend in recent weeks, with a T24 finish at the 3M Open and a T15 at the Rocket Classic, thanks to two specific tweaks. Working alongside his lifelong swing coach, Adam Harrell, Brennan shortened his backswing with his driver and focused specifically on his tempo with the putter. He ranked No. 3 in the field in strokes gained driving and No. 2 in the field in strokes gained putting at Sedgefield. Now a multiple-time winner on tour, Brennan can ride that momentum into the postseason, which begins with the FedEx Cup St. Jude Championship next week.

As Brennan closed out the win, an anxious Koivun waited in the clubhouse to watch his own postseason fate unfold after signing his scorecard for a tournament total of 8-under par, putting him in a tie for 29th place. After Brennan sank his final putt, it became official: Koivun made the playoffs on the number, ranked at No. 70 at the conclusion of the week.
